Figure 1:Frontend responsibility in an evolving FDB v3 request
(ecommerce_19; schematic). Execution can be offloaded, but
initiating a faithful request remains a frontend responsibility.
The user corrects both the product (laptop to tablet) and the
quantity (two to one);add_to_cartdepends on the product
ID returned bysearch_products.
(a) When domain schemas are available only to the backend,
the frontend may need successive hand-offs to convey the evolving
request, making it harder to preserve corrections and tool
dependencies.
(b) With schemas visible, Duopra can issue the corrected
domain-tool calls directly without a hand-off, whilequery(task)(\textit{task})remains available.
Crossed-out values and curved arrows denote superseded requests.
Table16(a) reports an observed delegated success
on this request.

Figure 2:Duopra’s three training stages on RV-Audio
(hjh_{j}: thinker hidden state at spoken-token positionjj;Pϕ0P_{\phi_{0}},PϕP_{\phi}: base and Stage-3 projectors;cjc_{j}: talker conditioning).
Stage 1 trains the thinker on unit-level sessions and yields Duopra-SFT (Table5).
Stage 2 trains a thinker LoRA with Dr. GRPO in the sandbox of Section4.3; Stage 2a yields Duopra-RL1 and Stage 2b yields Duopra-RL.
Stage 3 freezes the Duopra-RL thinker and trains only its projector, producing the final Duopra model.
